  p.how: One column per boot, the oldest at the left, and the letter below its number says how it ended: S a fatal hardware error ended it, p another panic, r the boot of the latest scan, - not on record. A cell gives the corrected errors of the boot as a number, U an uncorrected error, X an uncorrected error in a boot that stopped, ? a boot that stopped with no record naming a DIMM, - a DIMM that was not in the host. The table below holds the same.

  ## 3 Findings
  article#dimm-CPU0_C1.card.g-replace
    ### CPU0_C1 DDR5 RDIMM 64 GB 2Rx4 Example Memory EXM64G48R2X4-A S/N 3B9C56
    finding = replace now R-UE-01 1 uncorrected error, the latest on 2026-11-12 03:14 UTC at rank0 dev7 bg0 bank3 row 0x1a2f col 0x238 1 record
    evidence = R-ROW-03 row fault at rank0 dev7 bg0 bank3 row 0x1a2f: 421 errors in the last 7 days, 2.3 times the daily rate of the 30 days before 421 records R-REP-02 764 errors at rank0 dev7 bg0 bank3 row 0x1a2f after the hard PPR of 2026-10-28 765 records supports the other 15 DIMMs of this host have no unconfined errors: a cause in the board is unlikely
    repair = hard PPR at rank0 dev7 bg0 bank3 row 0x1a2f on 2026-10-28 01:30 UTC: 442 errors before, 764 after
    next = Replace the DIMM. Attach a case bundle of this DIMM to the return.
    p.sub: confidence high, 3 more statements, 2 checks not made, 2 kinds of data missing: the whole finding
    p.links: topology and address map timeline checks
  article#dimm-CPU1_D1.card.g-observe
    ### CPU1_D1 DDR5 RDIMM 64 GB 2Rx4 Example Memory EXM64G48R2X4-A S/N 2AEB41
    finding = observe R-SOFT-01 one cell fails repeatedly (rank0 dev17 bg5 bank3 row 0xa4e9 col 0x110): 53 errors since 2026-08-03, 2 in the last 7 days 53 records
    evidence = R-SOFT-01 the fault at rank0 dev17 bg5 bank3 row 0xa4e9 col 0x110 had errors in 4 of the last 4 boots
    next = No action. Look again when the count grows or a new place appears.
    p.sub: confidence medium: the whole finding
    p.links: topology and address map timeline checks
  p.how: The finding line gives the grade, the rule that set it and what that rule saw. Below stand at most three statements that bear on the decision: what the other rules saw, and checks that speak for the finding ("supports") or against it ("weakens"). A count of records leads to the records. The last line gives the confidence and counts what the whole finding in the appendix adds: further statements, checks that could not be made, missing data.
  ### Rules named in this report
  table.rules
    | rule | grade it gives | fires when
    | R-UE-01 | replace now | an uncorrected error on this DIMM
    | R-ROW-03 | consider replacement | the corrected errors of a row or column fault are rising or came in a recent burst, or its extent is spreading; or a fault covers a bank or more
    | R-REP-02 | consider replacement | errors came back at the same place after a repair
    | R-SOFT-01 | observe | corrected errors without a growing fault: stray errors at places that did not fail again, or a fault that is neither rising nor spreading

section#s6.sec
  ## 6 Checks against a wrong diagnosis
  p.how: Each finding was tested against causes outside the DIMM: the slot, the channel, the board, and slot names that disagree between sources. "supports" speaks for the finding and "weakens" against it. An open check could not be made from the records; where a person can settle it, the test is listed below the checks.
  section#check-dimm-CPU0_C1.dimm
    ### CPU0_C1 replace now
    #### Checks made from the records
    table.checks
      | result | check
      | open | no other DIMM on this channel: there is nothing to compare with
      | open | no slot move or reseat on record: a cause in the board is not ruled out
      | supports | the other 15 DIMMs of this host have no unconfined errors: a cause in the board is unlikely
    #### Tests for a person
    li: Swap the DIMM with one from another channel, or reseat it, and scan again after some days. The ledger then shows whether the errors follow the DIMM, stay in the slot or stop.
  section#check-dimm-CPU1_D1.dimm
    ### CPU1_D1 observe
    #### Checks made from the records
    p: The records gave no check for this finding.
    #### Tests for a person
    p: No test is open.
